chapter: Boston childhood, learning music and first gigs
title: Deciding to go to New York from an ice cream parlor
summary: Friends proposed a weekend trip to hear Hodges at the Savoy; only Holmes and Carney actually went, lying to their mothers and bringing altos and clarinets.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, how we decided to come to New York, I'll tell you. There was a bunch of us, Sunday afternoons, sitting in the ice cream parlor, which was where we all hung out. All the little girls come from Sunday School and one thing or another, and all us hip boys, you know, get 15 cents so you can get an ice cream soda -- one of them things. So we used to hang in this ice cream parlor all day.

And there were about five of us sitting at a table. So one of them says, "Hey, let's get together and go to New York on the weekend." We can go to the Savoy Ballroom, and Johnny Hodges is working over there." And man, when they said Johnny Hodges was there, I was for coming. Well, four of us decided to come over here; that is, myself, Harry Carney, another fellow named Edgar McIlvaine...
He was a drummer. And Johnny...Johnny... Johnny something... He was a guitar player. I forget what his last name is. There was four of us who were supposed to come over.

Well, we made a time and place; you know,, one of them things. So when it come time to go to, we come to find out there wasn't nobody coming except Harry and myself. So that was all right, too. Because I told my Mama I was going to stay with some friends of Harry's mother's, and he told his Mama the same thing, he was staying with some friends of my mother! Well, as it happened, did go to a friend of his mother's, you know, for a room, on Seventh Avenue, and she knew that he was coming or something. So she had a room, and we stayed there that night...
Now, you had a saxophone. Did Harry also have a saxophone?
Yeah, he had an alto. He was an alto player.
So the two of you had your altos...
Did you bring your clarinets? No...
Yeah. We didn't go anywhere without our instruments.
I see. So you brought both instruments.

I had a combination case. I always wondered, did I have the soprano in there...if I had one... I don't know if I had it then or not. But I had a combination case, and you know, I had my clarinet. Yeah, we had two altos, and we hit New York, and...
